claims.text: Content suitability sets how much sensitive content your Performance Max ads can sit next to on YouTube, Display and Google Video Partners. It is an account-level control, and it is easy to forget that it cannot be set per campaign or ad group.

claims.text: You choose one of three inventory types: Maximum, Moderate or Limited. YouTube and Display both default to Maximum.

claims.text: Maximum shows ads across all available inventory. It is still subject to content policies and automatically excludes highly sensitive content.

evidence.source_title: How to use brand suitability features in Performance Max

claims.text: Moderate excludes strong profanity, dramatized violence and sexually suggestive themes.

evidence.source_title: How to use brand suitability features in Performance Max

claims.text: Limited excludes as much sensitive content as possible, including moderate profanity and sexually suggestive themes, even in mainstream content such as music videos or makeup tutorials.

evidence.source_title: How to use brand suitability features in Performance Max

claims.text: Exclusions are applied on a best-efforts basis, so not every related placement is guaranteed to be blocked. Channel exclusions cannot be applied at ad group or campaign level.

claims.text: Use it when your brand has strict suitability requirements and you would rather give up some reach than risk appearing next to profanity, violence or suggestive themes.

claims.text: Do not rely on it when you need guaranteed blocking, or when you need different settings per campaign or ad group. It is account-level and best-efforts.

claims.text: Brand suitability risk: moving to Moderate or Limited may reduce the share of impressions on content you consider unsuitable. The trade-off is that a narrower inventory can cut reach and performance, so watch volume and CPA.

claims.text: Reach and conversion volume: Maximum may keep the widest delivery and the most conversion opportunity. The cost is greater exposure to mainstream content you may find borderline. This is an inference; the source does not give uplift figures.

relationships.name: Inventory filter for in-content ads
relationships.difference: Meta's filter sets the sensitivity of content next to in-content ads, which is close in purpose. It is documented only for Facebook in-stream reels and ads on Facebook Reels, whereas Google's setting covers YouTube, Display and Video Partners at account level.
relationships.context: Use when comparing content-sensitivity tiers across platforms; the scope of inventory differs.

relationships.name: Brand safety inventory filters
relationships.difference: Pinterest's filters help advertisers understand what content appears near their ads and see exposure levels. Pinterest does not show tiers that match Maximum, Moderate and Limited.
relationships.context: Useful as a brand safety reference point; do not assume the same tiers or controls.

relationships.name: Brand safety options (Smart+)
relationships.difference: TikTok offers brand safety options during placement setup in the upgraded Smart+ experience. TikTok does not describe tiers, and this is set in the campaign flow rather than as an account-level setting.
relationships.context: Related brand safety control in a different campaign setup flow.
